content: The nicotine patch is a transdermal delivery system approved by the FDA for managing withdrawal symptoms, including nicotine cravings, associated with smoking cessation. It is designed to provide a controlled release of nicotine into the bloodstream through the skin. Warnings and Precautions: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, use this medication only under the guidance of a healthcare provider. Smoking can harm your child, and while this medication is considered safer than smoking, the risks to your child are not fully understood. Do not use the nicotine patch if you continue to smoke, chew tobacco, use snuff, nicotine gum, or other nicotine-containing products. Consult a doctor before use if you have heart disease, a recent heart attack, or irregular heartbeat, as nicotine can increase heart rate. Similarly, consult a doctor if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, as nicotine can elevate blood pressure. Avoid use if you are allergic to adhesive tape or have skin problems, as this may increase the likelihood of developing rashes. If you are using a non-nicotine smoking cessation drug or taking prescription medications for depression or asthma, consult a doctor or pharmacist before use, as your prescription dose may need adjustment. Usage Instructions: Stop smoking completely when you begin using the patch. If you smoke more than 10 cigarettes per day, follow the recommended step-down schedule. If you smoke 10 or fewer cigarettes per day, start with Step 2 for six weeks, then Step 3 for two weeks, and then stop. Apply one new patch every 24 hours to clean, dry, hairless skin. Remove the backing and press the patch firmly onto the skin for 10 seconds. Wash your hands after applying or removing the patch. Dispose of used patches by folding the sticky sides together and placing them in the pouch provided. Rotate application sites daily to avoid skin irritation. Do not leave the patch on for more than 24 hours, as it may irritate the skin and lose effectiveness. If vivid dreams or sleep disturbances occur, remove the patch at bedtime and apply a new one in the morning. Do not cut the patch into smaller pieces or wear more than one patch at a time. Remove the patch before undergoing any MRI procedures to avoid potential burns. Stop using the patch after eight weeks. If you still feel the need to use it, consult your doctor. Contraindications: Do not use the nicotine patch if you continue to use other nicotine-containing products. Adverse Reactions: If skin redness caused by the patch does not resolve after four days, or if swelling or a rash develops, discontinue use and consult a doctor. Seek medical attention if you experience irregular heartbeat, palpitations, or symptoms of nicotine overdose, such as nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weakness, or rapid heartbeat. Special Populations: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of nicotine patches in pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance on use based on gender, race, or immunocompromised status. Storage: Store the patches at 20-25°C (68-77°F). Additional Notes: Alcohol interaction with nicotine patches has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol while using this medication. If you suspect an overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline immediately at 1-800-222-1222. The nicotine patch is a tool to aid smoking cessation, but it should be used responsibly and under the guidance of a healthcare provider to ensure safety and effectiveness.
